newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds slide with U.S., outperform peers.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds slide with U.S., outperform peers.

text.p: Argentine bonds finished sharply lower Friday in the wake of a slump in U.S. markets after strong U.S. economic indicator releases.
Both the U.S. jobs report and the National Association of Purchasing Managers Index released Friday led some players to think the U.S. Federal Reserve could adopt a more cautious monetary stance.
The U.S. 30-year yield rose 15 basis points to 6.45 percent.
But while Argentine bonds skidded with the U.S. markets, there was positive news in that Argentina outperformed peers Mexico and Brazil.
"I guess some people were hurt (by the slide) but nobody is really concerned," that the bullish trend will end, said a trader at a foreign bank.
Argentina's Par Brady bond dropped 1-1/4 to 74-3/4, while the dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 due 2001 was down $0.18 at 118.70.
Another trader said "the high values of bonds made it predictable that there would be some profit-taking, but the underlying tone remains firm."
The fact that Argentina outperformed Brazil and Mexico was largely thanks to the growing conviction that Moody's Investor Service is set to upgrade Argentina's credit-rating.

"The view (of an upgrade) really changed with the Ecuador rating," said the first trader. Recently Moody's assigned a B1 foreign currency rating to Ecuador, the same level as Argentina, something which led many players to think Argentina is set for an upgrade soon.
In the money markets, the three-month peso BAIBOR, the Buenos Aires inter-bank offered rate, was flat at 7.0625 percent.
